clue.text: Release captive sprite to behave without restraint

definitions.meaning: read as a whimsical phrase: let a pixie you hold prisoner go free, with 'one's elf' as the sprite in your keeping
to abandon all inhibition and act freely

explanation.surface: Someone frees an imprisoned fairy so that it can run riot.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a pun: split as LET ONE'S ELF GO, the phrase means freeing your own captive elf.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means abandoning self-control and acting with complete freedom.

clue.text: Intriguing, if cruel, devil

indicators.note: intriguing in the sense of plotting or scheming, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scheming, heartless demon is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' looks like an adjective meaning fascinating, but it signals an anagram of IF CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is a traditional name for Satan, the chief fallen angel.

clue.text: Let them oddly set upon girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, set upon places the first piece on top of the second
oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the word them are taken

parts.note: Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A gang strangely attacks a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' is a noun here, a lease or rental, not the verb. 'oddly' takes T and E from 'them'.
explanation.definitionFit: A let is a period of renting property, which is a tenancy.

clue.text: The state providing a change of clothing

definitions.meaning: a state of the USA on the east coast
a fresh pullover, read literally as a new jumper

explanation.surface: Someone asks which state supplies fresh clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A jersey is a knitted pullover; a new one is a change of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty United States, and literally a fresh jumper.

clue.text: Be sparing with millions hidden in a container

indicators.note: hidden in means the millions letter is tucked inside the container word

parts.note: a skip is a large open waste container
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A miser stashes a fortune in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: A SKIP is a British name for a large open rubbish container left on a street for building waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise or use too little of something.

clue.text: Young creature always allowed to go outside

indicators.note: the allowed word goes outside, wrapping round the always word

parts.note: allowed means let
always means ever

explanation.surface: A young animal is always permitted out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go outside' suggests a pet being let out into the garden, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare, a creature in its first year.

clue.text: Knight organised first celebration

indicators.note: first says the celebration word is placed first, before the organised word

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
had, as in had a party, means organised or held one

explanation.surface: A knight arranged the first party.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'organised, first celebration': HAD with GALA put first.
explanation.definitionFit: Galahad is the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Any left who'll get worried by inconspicuous observer?

indicators.note: letters that get worried are teased and disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Anyone on the left fears a discreet watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names someone who watches events unnoticed, like an insect on a wall.

clue.text: City endowed with prosperity these days

parts.note: luck in the sense of good fortune
these days means now, at present

explanation.surface: A city blessed with wealth in modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: LUCKNOW is a city in northern India.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh in India.

clue.text: Home with girl I had disabled

parts.note: to be home is to be in
Val is a girl's name
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone at home with a young woman describes themselves as disabled.
explanation.definitionFit: Invalid as an adjective describes someone weakened or disabled by illness.

clue.text: Frustrated girl's given job

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and the possessive gives Di's
appointed means given a post or job

explanation.surface: A frustrated woman has been handed a position.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is part of the wordplay here: Di's gives DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointed means let down or frustrated in one's hopes.

clue.text: Crime committed by receiver

parts.note: of can mean by, as in a work of Dickens
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: An offence carried out by someone handling stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' is the criminal sense: a FENCE handles stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of law, a crime.

clue.text: French soldier's horse captured by irregular troops

indicators.note: captured by means the horse letter is held inside the other piece
irregular means the letters of troops are put out of order

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A French soldier's mount is seized by guerrillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges TROOPS into PORTOS, and H (horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H) goes inside. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Porthos is one of Dumas's three musketeers, soldiers of the French king.

clue.text: A man of the cloth

parts.note: usually a clergyman, but read as a man's name that is also a looped towelling fabric

explanation.surface: A clergyman is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of the cloth' normally means a priest; split it into a man's name and a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry is a man's name and also a looped-pile cotton fabric used for towels.

clue.text: Began singing, initially with embellishments

indicators.note: with joins the first letter to what follows
initially takes the opening letter of the word singing

parts.note: tarted up means showily embellished or decorated

explanation.surface: A singer started off with flourishes.
explanation.walkthrough: TARTED UP is informal British for dressed up showily.
explanation.definitionFit: Started up is a phrasal verb meaning began or set going.

clue.text: These days elocution is a matter of habit

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, refers to the present era
diction is clarity of speech, elocution

explanation.surface: Nowadays clear speaking is just a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno Domini) marks our own era, hence 'these days'.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependency, a habit one cannot shake.

clue.text: A song the old man outside is discerning

indicators.note: the man word goes outside, enclosing the pieces that come before it

parts.note: Ed is a man's name
a glee is a part-song for unaccompanied voices
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Father sings outside and is sharp-sighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old man' looks like a father (DAD, PA), but it splits in two: an archaic article and a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagle-eyed means sharp-sighted, quick to notice detail.

clue.text: In the country one is brought in to tidy up the mess

indicators.note: brought in to means the one word goes inside the tidy up word

parts.note: to groom is to tidy up one's appearance
un is French for one, the country being France

explanation.surface: A villager is roped in to clear up the muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' is the naval sense: a GUNROOM is a mess for junior officers on a warship. 'In the country' points to France, where one is UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunroom is a shipboard mess, where junior naval officers eat.

clue.text: Previous title that's applied to queen

parts.note: an earl is a noble title
i.e. stands for id est, that is
R stands for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A former rank has been bestowed on a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means prior in time, previous.

clue.text: Antigua not the place to find fertiliser

indicators.note: the place to find says the answer can be found among the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Antigua is said not to be a source of manure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface claims the opposite of the truth: the letters run across 'Antigua not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is seabird or bat droppings used as fertiliser.

clue.text: Girl overcome by endless mourning for a relative

indicators.note: overcome by means the girl is surrounded by the mourning word
endless removes the last letter of the mourning word

parts.note: grief is mourning
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is overwhelmed by unceasing sorrow over a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final letter of the mourning word before it wraps round the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A grannie, or granny, is a grandmother, a family relative.

clue.text: Gymnast attaching label to whale as it surfaces

indicators.note: in a down clue, surfacing means rising, so the joined pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tab is a label
an orca is a killer whale

explanation.surface: A gymnast tags a whale as it comes up to breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: TAB joined to ORCA gives TABORCA; 'as it surfaces' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs gymnastic feats.

clue.text: Course where trainee comes unstuck

indicators.note: comes unstuck means the word trainee falls apart and is rebuilt

explanation.surface: A racecourse where an apprentice fails.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the racecourse near Liverpool that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous horse-racing course in Merseyside.

clue.text: Odds? Yes and no

parts.note: a betting price of one to one counts as odds, yet the word is the opposite of odd numbers

explanation.surface: Someone asked about the odds gives an equivocal answer.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, a one-to-one price is a kind of odds; but in numbers it is the opposite of odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is a betting price of one-to-one, and also means even numbers, not odd.

clue.text: Mortification of king subjected to restraint

indicators.note: subjected to restraint means the king is held within the restraint word

parts.note: a chain is a restraint
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A monarch is humiliated by being shackled.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of King George seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexed embarrassment or humiliation.

clue.text: Description of pride from 11th-century pope

definitions.meaning: a pride is a group of lions, so an adjective describing them
Pope Leo IX, pontiff from 1049 to 1054, with the Roman numeral spoken as a word

explanation.surface: A word for lions' pride comes from a medieval pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' is a lions' group, not vanity. Leo IX was pope 1049-54: LEO NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like or relating to lions.

clue.text: I belong working in base

indicators.note: working means the letters of I belong are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says they fit in at their workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a place of work but is the adjective meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means dishonourable, mean or base in character.

clue.text: It's time child, accompanied by me, invested in a stamp

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the child and me go into the stamp word

parts.note: an imprint is a stamp or mark
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A child and I have put money into a postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' is the prison sense, as in doing time; the surface's money investment is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing time means serving a prison sentence, so time is imprisonment.
